how: Indoor archery ranges with intro classes, lane rentals and leagues operate in Gowanus and the Lower East Side; NYC Parks rangers also run free archery on Staten Island.
The city's Harold Ickes Playground skate and BMX park in Red Hook opened in 2024; BMX-specific programming is limited.
VITAL and Brooklyn Boulders run indoor bouldering gyms with day passes and shoe rental.
Cricket is widely played on park pitches such as Van Cortlandt Park by the NYC Cricket League and community clubs; cricket became a varsity sport in city schools in 2008.
Tim Morehouse Fencing Club, Manhattan Fencing Center and New Amsterdam Fencing Academy run adult beginner classes with loaner gear.
New York GAA, founded 1914, fields hurling and Gaelic football teams that play at Gaelic Park in the Bronx.
Riding lessons and trail rides are available at Brooklyn and Bronx stables such as Kensington Stables beside Prospect Park.
Chelsea Piers Sky Rink runs year-round adult leagues and learn-to-play classes, and Central Park's Davis Center has an adult league.
Public skating is offered at Central Park's Wollman Rink, Bryant Park, Rockefeller Center and Chelsea Piers, with skate rental.
Central Rock Gym on the Upper West Side and Brooklyn gyms offer top rope, auto-belay and lead climbing with rentals.

how: Judo is taught in dojos such as Hoteikan Dojo in Bay Ridge and Staten Island Judo Jujitsu Dojo.
Padel Haus runs indoor padel courts in Brooklyn and Replay offers padel and pickleball.
CityPickle runs pay-to-play pickleball courts at Wollman Rink in Central Park, and indoor venues such as Replay exist.
Several amateur rugby union clubs play around the city, listed at nycrugby.com.
Free public skateparks include Pier 62, LES Skatepark under the Manhattan Bridge, Astoria Skate Plaza and Red Hook.
Big SNOW American Dream in East Rutherford, NJ, is an indoor real-snow slope with lesson programs; outdoor resorts are 1.5-2.5 hours away.
Taekwondo schools such as Ahns' Taekwondo NYC and West Side Taekwondo offer adult and kids classes.
GreenThumb supports hundreds of community gardens across the five boroughs where residents can join and garden plots.
Camping is possible at Floyd Bennett Field in Brooklyn (permit based) and at nearby state and county campgrounds.
Brooklyn Grange operates soil-based rooftop farms in Queens and the Brooklyn Navy Yard with farm visits and events.
Downtown Boathouse offers free walk-up kayaking on the Hudson at Pier 26 from May to October.
Ocean surfing with lessons and board rental is available at Rockaway Beach in Queens, reached by subway or ferry.
Mangroves do not grow in the New York climate; the nearest guided mangrove kayaking is in Florida, about a 2.5 hour flight.
